summary: # Marvelous Designer Learning Day: Sleeve Collection ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Jimmy from Marvelous Designer. Today, I will show you how to make a few types of sleeves. ## Lantern Sleeve ### Overview The first type of sleeve I will introduce is the lantern sleeve. This type of sleeve is relatively long. ### Steps to Create the Lantern Sleeve 1. **Adjust Length**: Begin by adjusting the length of the sleeve to make it longer overall. 2. **Cut the Sleeve**: Use the interlock to set an interlock and cut it off as a sleeve. 3. **Shrink the Sleeve**: After straightening it, slightly shrink the sleeve to allow the pleats to overlap at the sleeve position. 4. **Set Elasticity**: Apply 100% elasticity for the sleeve and adjust its proportion to 100. This helps maintain the original length of the line and prevents it from being easily stretched. ### Additional Adjustments - If you have any questions later, I will answer them in the Q&A section. - Use the extension tool to add fabric to the sleeve and determine where the center of the sleeve is. Add a straight line to mark the center. - Switch to the extension tool, click on one side of the sleeve, then click on the other side and the middle line of the extension to extend from the middle to both sides. ### Finalizing the Lantern Sleeve - Freeze the sleeve to avoid effects on the garment. - Adjust the sleeve's length to ensure consistency. - Use pressure settings to create a slight sense of fluttering. ## Road Shoulder Embroidery ### Overview The second type of sleeve is the road shoulder embroidery. ### Steps to Create the Road Shoulder Embroidery 1. **Create Loop Line**: Make a loop line in the position of the mountain and set a longer board. 2. **Cut and Delete**: Cut the long board out and delete the shoulder board to show the shoulder of the model. 3. **Use Extension Tool**: Extend the board for more fabric and wrinkles on the sleeves. 4. **Adjust Curves**: Ensure the curve is smooth by adjusting the board. ### Finalizing the Road Shoulder Embroidery - Activate the thinner board and apply 100% elasticity to maintain the original length. - Use the selection grid tool to add detail to the fabric by increasing the density of the grid. ## Closing Sleeve ### Overview The third sleeve is the closing sleeve, which requires a lot of folds. ### Steps to Create the Closing Sleeve 1. **Set Up Lines**: Make sure the sleeve is long enough to have enough fabric for folds. 2. **Align Lines**: Select all lines and align them to the outside of the panel before adding points. 3. **Symmetrical Panel**: If the two sides are symmetrical, set up a symmetrical panel to edit one side at a time. 4. **Fold and Adjust**: After extending the panel, delete any not smooth lines and adjust curves as needed. ### Finalizing the Closing Sleeve - Set elasticity for the top of the panel line to create folds. - Adjust the position of the sleeve to ensure more folds. ## Non-Sew Sleeve ### Overview The fourth sleeve is a non-sew sleeve. ### Steps to Create the Non-Sew Sleeve 1. **Draw Panel**: Draw a rectangular panel and add a long strip. 2. **Adjust Shape**: Make the shape of this panel look more natural by adjusting the curve. 3. **Apply Elasticity**: Apply 100% elasticity to avoid the sleeve being too long. ### Finalizing the Non-Sew Sleeve - Reduce particle diameter to refine details. - Adjust the curve for a more aesthetically pleasing design. ## Gourd Sleeve ### Overview The next sleeve is the gourd sleeve. ### Steps to Create the Gourd Sleeve 1. **Set Inner Lines**: Set several inner lines based on the flat surface line curve. 2. **Add Points**: Add points to adjust the flat surface later. 3. **Turn into Curve Line**: Convert the lines into a curve line and unify the left side. ### Finalizing the Gourd Sleeve - Simulate and adjust the shape for a natural look. - Use the extension tool to widen the sleeve. ## Electric Shoulder Sleeve ### Overview The next sleeve is the electric shoulder sleeve. ### Steps to Create the Electric Shoulder Sleeve 1. **Raise Sleeve Height**: Increase the overall sleeve height. 2. **Set Vertical Sleeve Line**: Create a vertical sleeve line based on the curve. 3. **Use Extension Tool**: Extend the inner line. ### Finalizing the Electric Shoulder Sleeve - Adjust the curve for a more natural appearance. - Apply a harder fabric to enhance structure. ## Calf Sleeve ### Overview The calf sleeve is another design I will demonstrate. ### Steps to Create the Calf Sleeve 1. **Raise Sleeve Height**: Adjust the overall sleeve height for ample fabric. 2. **Create Seam**: Cut from the side of the fabric and set shapes. 3. **Use Extension Tool**: Extend the leg sleeve for more fabric to create folds. ### Finalizing the Calf Sleeve - Sew up the panels and observe the sewing line in the 3D window. ## Sewing Methods ### Overview I will introduce two types of sewing methods. ### Simple Frame Tells 1. **Lengthen Board**: Lengthen the board by pressing the Shift key for separate width and height adjustments. 2. **Internal Line Generation**: Generate the internal line based on the curve line. 3. **Fold Line Tool**: Use the fold line tool to create folds. ### Complicated Method 1. **Draw Internal Shape**: Create the necessary internal shape for folds. 2. **Adjust and Copy**: Adjust the shape and copy it to create layers. 3. **Sew Up Layers**: Sew the layers correctly to maintain the design. ## Conclusion Thank you for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to ask in the chat. You can also join our official support group for further assistance. The group number is at the bottom left corner of the screen, and the password is HANA.
